papers.title: Improved rapid phase ordering for Ising dynamics on random regular graphs
papers.abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for the Ising model on random $d$-regular graphs with $n$ vertices at low temperature, in the regime $\beta \geq C/d$ where $C,d$ are sufficiently large constants. In this regime, the full mixing time is exponential in $n$, because of the bottleneck between the two dominant phases: configurations with a majority of plus spins and configurations with a majority of minus spins. We show that, for sufficiently large $d$, if the dynamics is initialized with an excess of at least $\epsilon_{C,d} n$ plus spins over minus spins, then it quasi-equilibrates in time $O(\log n)$ to the Gibbs measure conditioned on positive magnetization. In addition, the required bias $\epsilon_{C,d}$ can be chosen so that $\epsilon_{C,d}\to 0$ as $d,C\to\infty$. Previous bound of \cite{GSS25+} in the Ising and large-$d$ setting required $\beta \gtrsim (\log d)/d$. A key difficulty is that, even from the all-plus initialization, one must control the propagation of negative information in spacetime in a low-temperature model with strong local correlations. We address this by developing a new bootstrap approach to proving subcriticality of disagreement clusters under the grand coupling.

papers.title: A mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy
papers.abstract: Foraging recruitment is a contagion: an agent that finds a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade, the model built for rumour and adoption spread on social networks, now embedded in space. Because activation is degree-normalized, the same rule that spreads the cascade also stifles it as neighbourhoods crowd, so the swarm aggregates on a resource and then releases to explore again. The cascade runs on the communication network, but acting on it moves agents in physical space, and that motion rewires the network: network and space are one coupled system, and this feedback, not any tuning, makes the coordination self-limiting. Because recruitment chains along the graph rather than reaching near neighbours alone, whether a discovery stays local or spans the swarm is a question of percolation. The swarm holds itself in a cascade window that is locally near-critical though globally subcritical, a self-organized, self-limiting drive-release cycle, sandpile-like but non-conservative. Nothing is tuned, yet behaviours that foraging biology documents separately emerge together: recruitment to discoveries, marginal-value patch-leaving, and Levy search with a switch to local exploitation. These follow from one least-committal principle, the resource field and the search both as maximum entropy, with Levy search matched to the field's sparsity and recruitment to its clustering, so active-matter order and optimal foraging appear as one system seen in two domains. The gains are real but conditional: up to 7.6x the harvest of solitary search when resources are sparse and clustered, shrinking to nothing when search is already easy. That sparse, clustered field is also the generic one, because resources almost inevitably aggregate, so one untuned rule should recur widely.

papers.title: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
papers.abstract: We introduce a two-stage data-driven neural framework for discovering dynamically admissible extreme scenarios. Rather than assuming prior knowledge of the governing equations, the first stage infers the effective dynamical constraints directly from observational data. When the underlying physical system possesses suitable symmetries, the learned dynamics can be represented in a geometry-agnostic form, independent of any fixed grid, coordinate system, dimensionality, and intrinsic curvature. In the second stage, a physics-informed neural-search uses this learned dynamics to uncover rare, high-impact coherent structures that may not have appeared in the original observations. We demonstrate this framework through representative examples of increasing dimensionality and geometric complexity. Starting from a traditionally learned Duffing dynamics, we find a homoclinic pulse as a plausible localized extreme scenario. Next, since the same equation also appears in the stationary nonlinear Schrodinger system, with the coordinate interpreted as space instead of time, this pulse becomes a standing soliton. We then retrain the first stage using a geometry-agnostic neural representation, enabling the learned dynamics to be lifted to higher-dimensional space to obtain higher-dimensional solitary profile, known as Townes soliton. Finally, with a Liouville system, we demonstrate that dynamics learned from data on a (1+1)-dimensional Lorentzian quasi-manifold can be transferred to a (2+0)-dimensional Euclidean manifold to identify an instanton. Our approach can be applied to other coherent spatiotemporal structures, including kinks, rogue waves, compactons, peakons, and potentially even singularities, with applications in risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection.

papers.title: Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
papers.abstract: We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.

papers.title: Strichartz Estimates and Scattering for the Massless Reduced Dirac-Fock Equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish Strichartz estimates for the reduced Dirac-Fock equation for 3D massless spinors, linearized around non-localized equilibria. Our analysis covers both the random field and the density matrix frameworks. As an application, we deduce scattering for the corresponding nonlinear problem with a high-frequency cut-off.

papers.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, I: radiation conditions and a Rellich-type theorem
papers.abstract: We study the negative Laplacian on the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$, $n \ge 3$, subject to a constant impedance (Robin) boundary condition with $\alpha > 0$. The boundary then carries a bound transverse mode, and at each energy $E > 0$ the system propagates two channels with the distinct wavenumbers $\sqrt{E}$ and $\sqrt{E+\alpha^2}$: bulk waves decaying like $|x|^{-(n-1)/2}$ and surface waves decaying like $|x'|^{-(n-2)/2}$. The two rates are not comparable pointwise. Each is critical for the Agmon-H\"ormander space $\mathcal{B}^*$, however. This Part I treats the flat boundary, and its purpose is to develop, at that endpoint, the scattering theory of the two channels in full. We prove a limiting absorption principle $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}^*$, construct the generalized Fourier transform, derive an expansion of the resolvent at infinity in which the two channels appear in a single relation, characterize the solutions of $\mathcal{B}^*$ growth, and compute the scattering matrix. The radiation condition is imposed on the solution itself, with no decomposition into channels, and is shown to be equivalent to the vanishing of the incoming data. The main result is a Rellich-type theorem whose hypotheses are imposed only near infinity and which forces both channels to vanish simultaneously. The surface channel turns out to be rigid: its block of the scattering matrix is the identity and carries no information about $\alpha$, so that on the band $-\alpha^2 < E < 0$ the scattering matrix is trivial. The bulk block, by contrast, determines $\alpha$.

papers.title: On Nonlocal Equations under Symmetries
papers.abstract: In this work, we establishes results of existence and regularity for solutions to nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u(x)) ~\text{and}~f(\Delta_{g})u=U(x,u(x))$ in the Euclidean context and Riemannian context respectively. We extend the results of \cite{Gorka 6} for the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ under cylindrically symmetry and compact Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ under action of a closed Lie subgroup $G \leq \text{Isom}_{g}(M)$. Our approach combines spectral theory, complex interpolation and fixed-point methods.

papers.title: Local well-posedness of wave kinetic equations associated with water waves
papers.abstract: We prove two conceptually different local well-posedness results for wave kinetic equations associated with water-wave systems. For pure gravity waves with 2D interfaces, we establish a classical well-posedness theory in weighted Sobolev spaces: regularity is propagated, and solutions depend continuously on the initial data in the same topology. For gravity-capillary waves with one-dimensional interfaces, the situation is fundamentally different. We prove well-posedness in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces (in the sense of existence, uniqueness, and continuity in a weaker topology), but we also show that, in general, any additional regularity of the initial data is instantly lost. Moreover, continuity in time and continuous dependence on the initial data fail in the weighted $L^\infty$ norm, even for smooth compactly supported initial data. This instability is caused by degenerate three-wave resonances, which produce singular collision rates and arbitrarily short relaxation time scales. The distinction between the two theories reflects a fundamental difference in their resonant geometry.

papers.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
papers.abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(\Delta_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.

papers.title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.

papers.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
papers.abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.

papers.title: Matrix divisors, Christoffel transformations and symmetric $d$-connections
papers.abstract: The Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ relates elementary bundle modifications to gap probability recurrences. The moment matrix determines normalization and the splitting type. We define the source and target moduli problems by their local data. The modifications identify common stable loci and conjugate their point-addition maps. For Pearson ratios $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\deg d=1,2$, we construct rational spectral coordinates and compute the induced transformation. For positive even weights with finite moments, reweighting configurations yields the transformed gap probability recurrence. Its coefficient is a rational function of the transformed spectral coordinates. A local formula applies outside these charts under the stated hypotheses.

papers.title: Quantization in polarization via transverse Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt theorem
papers.abstract: We construct, for every prequantizable symplectic manifold $(M,\omega,L)$ equipped with a nonsingular polarization, a deformation quantization $(C_M^\infty[[\hbar]],\star)$ together with a filtered sheaf of subalgebras $C_{M,\hbar}^{(<\infty)}$ that admits an exact action on polarized sections of $L^{\otimes k}$ for each $k\in\mathbb Z^+$. This extends the Kostant--Souriau action of polarization-preserving functions. The main geometric ingredient is a transverse PBW theory associated with a Nirenberg integrable distribution $P$. For any locally free $P$-modules $E$ and $E'$, we construct a PBW isomorphism for the bundle of transverse differential operators from $E$ to $E'$. This extends the PBW theorem for Lie pairs of Laurent-Gengoux--Sti\'enon--Xu to the setting of $P$-modules. After specializing $\hbar= \tfrac{\sqrt{-1}}{k}$, we obtain a sheaf $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ of level-$k$ quantizable functions and prove that its action identifies $O_k^{(<\infty)}$ with the sheaf of transverse differential operators on $L^{\otimes k}$. In the K\"ahler case, this recovers the construction of Chan--Leung--Li. Finally, for standard symplectic tori with real polarizations, we compare our construction with Toeplitz-type operators and obtain their semiclassical asymptotic expansions.

papers.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
papers.abstract: The Anderson tight-binding model is a fundamental model of quantum transport and localization in disordered media. Solving a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig, this paper proves Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential, in any dimension $d\ge 2$. The proof uses the multiscale framework of Fr\"ohlich-Spencer and Bourgain-Kenig, and the main new ingredient is a probabilistic discrete unique continuation principle (PDUC) for the discrete Schr\"odinger equation. This PDUC is established via a bootstrap argument and a key probabilistic lemma proved by adaptively revealing the random potential.

papers.title: Stability and instability for particle dynamics in magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We study zero-speed equilibria of the Newton-Lorentz equation $\ddot x=\dot x\times B(x)$ in $\mathbf{R}^3$, which describes the motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field $B$. We prove Lyapunov instability wherever the field $B$ does not vanish (under $C^1$ regularity), and at every isolated zero of $B$ provided it is real-analytic. These results do not assume that the field is divergence-free. In contrast, we construct a compactly supported divergence-free $C^\infty$ field that is flat at an isolated zero and makes the corresponding equilibrium Lyapunov stable.

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies with positive masses
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every choice of positive masses, the planar Newtonian five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to similarity. After normalization and removal of the translation and rotation freedoms, every physical configuration is isolated in the complex solution variety. The proof combines the classification of singular sequences by Albouy and Kaloshin with a lower bound for the potential, asymptotic estimates, and local analytic reductions.

papers.title: Strictly convex ergodic billiards
papers.abstract: We produce the first known strictly convex ergodic billiards: sufficiently asymmetric lemon billiards. These billiard tables are the intersection of two circles of which one contains the centers of both. We previously proved that they have \emph{uniformly} hyperbolic returns to a suitable section, and we here control singularity curves, with an approach that seems new. This implies ergodicity and indeed the Bernoulli property.

papers.title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations
papers.abstract: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.

papers.title: Polynomial Spectral Gap Estimates for Finitely Differentiable Quasi-Periodic Schr\"odinger Operators
papers.abstract: We prove polynomial upper bounds on spectral gaps of quasi-periodic Schr\"odinger operators with small $C^{k}$ potentials and Diophantine frequencies. For sufficiently large $k$, the decay exponent is $k-34\tau$, where $\tau$ is the Diophantine exponent. We construct examples with lower bounds along infinitely many gap labels, showing that the leading coefficient $1$ of $k$ is asymptotically optimal. The proof uses quantitative reducibility and the Moser-P\"oschel argument.

papers.title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
papers.abstract: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $\theta=\beta/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $N\theta\to\gamma>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/\theta$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $\gamma$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $\beta$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $\gamma\to\infty$.

papers.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
papers.abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

papers.title: Invariant pseudo-unitary matrix ensembles and local statistics and conductance fluctuations of the DMPK ensemble
papers.abstract: We consider the DMPK ensemble, which models quantum transport in a disordered wire, and describe its limiting local statistics as the number of particles tends to infinity. In the metallic regime, as well as at crossover I, we obtain sine statistics in the bulk, Bessel statistics at the hard edge and Airy statistics at the soft edge. In the insulating regime, we prove localization around certain explicit deterministic positions with Gaussian fluctuations. This confirms and quantifies the predicted universal and localized behavior in the physics literature. At crossover II, we obtain explicit limiting kernels in the bulk and at both edges, which interpolate between these regimes. The hard edge kernel involves Legendre functions and, to the best of our knowledge, is new, while the bulk and soft edge kernels agree with those derived for the squared singular values of critically scaled products of independent Ginibre matrices. To explain these similarities, we construct a class of invariant pseudo-unitary matrices that is closed under taking products and use it to interpret the DMPK ensemble as the joint density of the spectral variables of a product of such random matrices. More generally, the latter takes the form of a polynomial ensemble of derivative type involving a second order differential operator compatible with the Legendre functions. Finally, we obtain uniform asymptotic expansions of the mean and variance of the conductance and prove that the DMPK ensemble admits universal conductance fluctuations, i.e. the variance of the conductance tends to $1/15$ throughout the whole metallic regime. This again confirms the predictions in the physics literature.

papers.title: The ABC-equation revisited: missed (quasi) integrable cases. Part II: extensions and actions
papers.abstract: We continue here the study of the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$ and using the results obtained in the first part construct new quasi-integrable structures and compute their actions on symmetries and cosymmetries.

papers.title: Simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets
papers.abstract: Visibility from the origin in integer lattices is a well-studied problem. More recently, the corresponding question for cut-and-project sets has attracted attention. We consider simultaneous visibility, which asks what points in a set are visible from every point of another set. This question was studied for the integer lattice by Rearick and Rumsey, among others. In this work, we investigate simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets associated with real quadratic fields satisfying the Hammarhjelm condition. Under suitable geometric conditions on the finite set, we prove that the density of the simultaneously visible points exists and derive an explicit formula for it. We also examine simultaneous visibility in more general cut-and-project sets under a condition on the associated lattice.

papers.title: Lower bounds for self-adjoint Sturm-Liouville operators
papers.abstract: In this note we provide estimates for the lower bound of the self-adjoint operator associated with the three-coefficient Sturm-Liouville differential expression $$ \frac{1}{r} \left(-\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx} p \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dx} + q\right) $$ in the weighted $L^2$-Hilbert space $L^2(\mathbb R; rdx)$.

papers.title: An alternating Mizuno formula, modified gamma functions, and double sine special values
papers.abstract: For $n\ge1$ and $\operatorname{Re}(x_j)>0$, we prove an alternating analogue of Mizuno's product formula: \begin{equation*} \prod\nolimits_{m=0}^{\infty} \left(\prod_{j=1}^{n}(m+x_j)\right)^{(-1)^m} = \frac{(\sqrt{\pi/2})^n} {\prod_{j=1}^{n}\widetilde{\Gamma}(x_j)}, \end{equation*} where $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is the modified gamma function associated with the alternating Hurwitz zeta function. The polynomial factors are regularized using factorwise logarithms, and the formula establishes compatibility between this regularization and polynomial factorization. Applications include Gaussian and cyclotomic (Kurokawa--Wakayama type) evaluations; the single-factor case recovers the alternating Lerch formula, and a normalized ratio yields Wallis' product. A second group of results concerns an alternating double sine-type function. At nonexceptional positive periods, its positive-integer special values admit finite tangent-product representations. These products define locally meromorphic continuations $F_m$ in the period parameter. For $m\ge2$ and nonzero algebraic parameters, the continued values belong to $\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ at rational parameters and are finite, nonzero, and transcendental at nonrational parameters. We determine their orders at rational parameters and distinguish parameter continuation from fixed-period specialization at exceptional parameters. Additional results include Barnes factorizations of multiple alternating gamma functions, a Glaisher--Kinkelin special value, finite-product Stirling-type asymptotics, a symmetric two-parameter form of the known odd-integer multiplication formula, and an odd-scaling distribution relation for the alternating double sine-type function.

papers.title: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the norm properties of quantum uniformity measures, introduced by Bu, Gu, and Jaffe to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. Resolving an open question they posed, we show that quantum uniformity measures define norms precisely for $k=2,3,4$. In particular, we establish the triangle inequality for $k=4$, whereas for every $k\geq5$ it fails in some dimension. The higher-order result is proved using the structure theory of norming systems of linear equations over finite fields. We also study the geometry of quantum uniformity measures, establishing explicit bounds on the modulus of convexity whenever they define norms. Finally, we give a complete classification of the norm properties of matrix-valued Gowers uniformity functionals, showing that only $k=2$ defines a norm.

papers.title: Boundary One-Point Functions in the Open XXZ Spin Chain with Generic Integrable Boundaries
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.

papers.title: Analytical solution of electromagnetic heating in a stratified absorbing medium
papers.abstract: We consider the temperature evolution in a skin tissue when it is exposed to an electromagnetic wave. The heating is caused by the absorbed power as the electromagnetic wave attenuates inside the skin. In many applications, the characteristic depth of attenuation is small in comparison with the lateral size of the electromagnetic beam. Because of this separation of length scales, the lateral heat conduction is negligible at leading order. Previously, we studied electromagnetic heating in a skin of a single homogeneous layer. We derived the leading-term analytical solution and the asymptotic corrections up to the second order for lateral heat conduction and for oblique incidence. In this study, we derive the analytical solution in the case of perpendicular incidence on a stratified skin tissue with a layer-specific profile for electromagnetic attenuation. It should be emphasized that in the current study, the heat capacity and conductivity are still uniform over the entire skin tissue; only the electromagnetic attenuation is stratified resulting in a layer-specific heating profile.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture
papers.abstract: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian $H^{v,\mathbf{A}}$ has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian $H^{v,-\mathbf{A}}$, with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge $\pm 1/2$. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.
